veranderings.voor: By elke materiaal hieronder lees jy van sy eienskappe
veranderings.na: Hieronder lees jy oor elke materiaal se eienskappe
veranderings.rede: 'By elke materiaal ... lees jy van' is wooden; 'lees jy oor ... se eienskappe' is the natural construction.
The contrast reads more naturally as an appended phrase after a comma than joined with 'en'.

veranderings.voor: Mense vul daarom gate in 'n muur met gips en maak die muur glad.
veranderings.na: Mense gebruik daarom gips om gate in 'n muur te vul en die muur glad te maak.
veranderings.rede: 'gate in 'n muur met gips' can be misread as 'a wall with plaster'; the rewording keeps the meaning and removes the ambiguity.
The sentence compares a concrete wall, so the comparison should be with a wooden wall, not with wood in general.

veranderings.voor: 'n Mens maak nie 'n voorwerp uit verf nie
veranderings.na: 'n Mens maak nie 'n voorwerp van verf nie
veranderings.rede: The lesson says 'van ... gemaak' everywhere else; using 'van' here as well keeps it consistent.
'uitdroog' suggests drying out or parching; paint simply dries, and it 'forms' a layer rather than 'becoming' one.
'die ding' is vague and too casual; 'oppervlak' names what lies under the paint layer.
With 'baie skole' and 'die vensters' the plural 'vloere' is the natural parallel; the protected 'By baie skole' stays as it is.

vlae.teks: In die gemeenskap is sypaadjies dikwels van beton en klinieke se mure met verf beskerm.
vlae.rede: The single 'is' does duty for both parts of the sentence, so it is unclear whether 'dikwels' also applies to the clinics' walls. Spelling that out would decide the qualifier, so the writer should settle it.

vlae.teks: Glas is hard en waterdig, en 'n mens kan gewoonlik dwarsdeur glas sien.
vlae.rede: Not a safety flag. The protected entry for 'vensterglas is hard en waterdig' lists 'glas is hard en waterdig' as withdrawn because glass fibre bends, and that general wording appears here. A language change cannot fix it, so I have left it unchanged for the writer or a person to judge.
